properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:31PM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the San Juan River caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...along the San Juan River from the Four Corners through
Mexican Hat, UT. This includes Bluff, Montezuma Creek and Aneth.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST, stream gauge reports upstream and impacts of
flooding have been reported along the San Juan River near
Farmington, NM. Expect flood waters to reach the Four Corners
Wednesday evening and the town of Bluff early Thursday morning.
Timing of crest is subject to change as more details become
available. Please continue to monitor the forecast and updated
warnings.
- At 11:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 22 feet late this evening with
a secondary crest near 23.5 feet expected near Bluff early
Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Bluff, Montezuma Creek, and Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 558 AM MST, water levels near Woodruff and Holbrook have
fallen below flood stage with no additional rises expected. Water
levels at Winslow remain above moderate flood stage, and
additional rises to above major flood stage will be possible
through the day today. Flooding will continue to remain a threat
downstream of Winslow in the Birdsprings area as well. Flooding
is already ongoing.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 5:00am MST the stage was 23.18 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Additional rises over 25.0 feet are possible through
the day.
Impacts:
At 22.0 feet: Lowland flooding on right bank. Damage on left bank
to Ames Acres and Bushman Acres in the event of levee failure.
At 25.0 feet: Levee is overtopped. Major flooding of portions of
Winslow including Ames Acres and Bushman Acres.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Winslow, Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi
Ruins State Park and Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 3 at 2:05AM MST until November 3 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Havasu Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 900 AM MST Tuesday.

* At 205 AM MST, a river gauge on Cataract Creek reported a rapid
rise of 5.38 feet as a result of heavy rain far upstream. A flood
wave is traveling through Cataract/Havasu Creek. Estimated time for
impacts to begin at Supai is between 9 AM to noon MST, though this
may change. Stay tuned to future updates for refinements on this
estimate.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Havasu Creek basin.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Havasu Creek basin.

* For Cataract Creek at Cataract Creek Below Heather Wash:
At 1:30am the stage was 4.46 feet.
Flood Stage is 7.5 feet.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: 450 cfs flow. May cause minor flooding downstream in
Supai campground 4 to 7 hours later.
At 10.0 feet: 1520 cfs flow. May cause moderate flooding downstream
in Suapi village 4 to 7 hours later.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Supai, Havasupai Reservation, Little Navajo Falls, Mooney Falls and
Beaver Falls.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Very Last Chance Camp Site.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes on Havasu Creek near Supai.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Heather Wash, Sinyella Canyon, Little Coyote Canyon, Pasture Wash,
Havasu Creek, Black Tank Wash, Colorado River and Coconino Wash.
properties.instruction:
Campers and hikers should hustle to higher ground immediately! Stay
away from creeks and washes!

Foot bridges will be washed out in Supai Campground. Some campsites
will be flooded. Campers may be stranded in portions of the
campground.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 2:07AM MST until November 4 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Animas River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Animas River at Farmington.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, major flooding is occurring along the lower
Animas River. Water levels are approaching those experienced during
the great flood of October 1911.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 AM MST Tuesday the stage was 13.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 AM MST Tuesday was 13.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is near crest and is expected to fall below
flood stage around midnight and continue falling.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at noon MST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL WEDNESDAY MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL; Indian River, FL; Martin, FL; St. Lucie, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 9:15PM EST until November 3 at 9:30AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Eastern Indian River County in east central Florida...
Northeastern Martin County in east central Florida...
St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. It will take
several hours for all the water from the heavy rain that has
already fallen to work through local drainage systems in urban
areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 914 PM EST, Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated additional
downpours developing and moving over already saturated ground.
- This replaces the existing Flood Warning. If heavy rain persists,
additional Flash Flood Warnings may be required overnight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Saint Lucie, Palm Bay, Melbourne, Walton, Fort Pierce,
Sebastian, Stuart, Vero Beach, Satellite Beach, Fellsmere, Indian
River Shores, Malabar, Indialantic, Vero Beach South, Gifford,
Winter Beach, Wabasso, Sebastian Highlands and Roseland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:49PM MST until November 3 at 12:45PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1245 PM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding continues on the Vamori Wash. The Vamori Wash
has risen to 9.85 feet and the Highway 21 bridge approaches flood
and the road may be impassible above 9.80 feet.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1243 PM MST, Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Vamori Wash.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Santa Cruz and Kupk.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 8:39PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused a rise in the river levels on the St.
Johns River near Above Lake Harney. The river is forecast to climb
through Minor flood stage and into Moderate flood stage over the next
few days. Rises near Major flood stage will be possible this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Flooding of homes in low lying areas
becomes more significant. Many secondary roads are impassable,
limiting access to homes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue rising to 9.8 feet Saturday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 1145 AM EST.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in New

San Juan River At Shiprock affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Significant impacts are likely in the Shiprock area and
along the San Juan River from Shiprock to the Four Corners.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 AM MST Tuesday the stage was 19.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:00 AM MST Tuesday was 19.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.5 feet
this morning. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:29PM MST until November 6 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa County.

.Minor flooding along the Rio Grande through Alamosa is expected due
to upstream flooding occurring in the vicinity of Monte Vista.

For the Rio Grande...including Alamosa...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon to late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM MST Monday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Wednesday afternoon to a crest of 9.6 feet late Wednesday
evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Thursday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

This warning will be in effect until the river falls below its flood
stage.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM MST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON TO LATE THURSDAY NIGHT... ...REPLACES RIVER FLOOD WATCH

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 10:02PM MST until November 3 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks. These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 PM MST Monday the stage was 6.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:00 PM MST Monday was 6.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.3 feet
late this evening. It will then fall below flood stage late
tonight.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.3
feet on 04/25/2008.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
